title: Excel for Service Delivery
subtitle: From reading a raw export to presenting a one-page dashboard, on real call-center data.
languageLabel: Egyptian Arabic narration, English Excel terms
description: Four recorded live sessions from Kalam CX's Workforce Management team, cut into short chapters you can watch one at a time. The trainer works in Excel on a real-style call-center export, explaining in Egyptian Arabic with the English Excel terms you see on screen.

Start with the short course: one animated quick video for each of the first three sessions. Each full session then has the trainer's live demos; Sessions 1 to 3 add practice in the Activities Workbook and a short self-marking test, and Session 4 works through an assessment with the trainer. A 20-task practical exam closes the course.
outcomes: Read any system export: find the header row, the data range and each column's type
Answer manager questions with SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, MAX, MIN and their IFS versions
Lock references with $ and F4 so formulas copy correctly
Split dates and times for weekly and interval (WFM) reports
Look values up with VLOOKUP, HLOOKUP and XLOOKUP
Clean a messy export: Remove Duplicates, Text to Columns, Flash Fill, LEFT/RIGHT/MID, Data Validation
Summarise thousands of rows with PivotTables, calculated fields, slicers and PivotCharts
Pull IDs and dates out of text with LEFT, RIGHT and MID, and match values with COUNTIFS and INDEX/MATCH
requirements: Microsoft Excel 2016 or later. Microsoft 365 is best: XLOOKUP needs Excel 2021 or 365.
Comfortable with spoken Egyptian Arabic; Excel menus and functions are shown in English
audience: Service delivery team leaders and supervisors
WFM and reporting analysts who are new to Excel
New hires in onboarding who work with call-center data

lessons.title: Session test
lessons.note: Formulas here use commas (,) between arguments and a dot for decimals. If your Excel uses semicolons (;) and decimal commas, which is common with Arabic or European regional settings, type those instead.

questions.q: A WFM export has a report title in rows 1-2, column names in row 4, 20 agents in rows 5-24 and "End of export." in row 25. Which row is the header row?
questions.e: The header row is the single row of column names. Title lines above it and the footer below are not data.

questions.q: The Shift column shows "09:00 - 18:00". What type is it for Excel?
questions.e: The dash makes it text. Excel cannot calculate with it as a time (unlike Login Time 09:02).

questions.q: A number is left-aligned and has a small green triangle. What does it mean?
o: It is a number stored as text
questions.e: Numbers align right by default. A left-aligned number with a green triangle is stored as text, and SUM will ignore it.

questions.q: Manager: "What is the longest AHT in the team (the slowest agent)?" Which function?
questions.e: For AHT the worst value is the biggest, so MAX.

questions.q: Manager: "What is the lowest Service Level % in the team?" Which function?
questions.e: For Service Level the worst value is the smallest, so MIN.

questions.q: You need to count the agent NAMES in column B. Which function?
questions.e: COUNT counts numbers only (it gives 0 on names). COUNTA counts any non-empty cell.

questions.q: 20 agents, but 2 new joiners have a blank Service Level. What does =COUNT(H53:H72) return?
questions.e: COUNT ignores blank cells: 20 − 2 = 18.

questions.q: =B2/B5 is copied down to calculate each agent's share of the team total in B5, and the results break. What is the fix?
questions.e: The team total must stay locked. Press F4 to add the $ signs.

questions.q: Which argument order is correct for SUMIFS?
questions.e: SUMIF puts the sum range last; SUMIFS puts it first because it can take up to 127 conditions.

questions.q: Nour Hassan: 405 calls offered, 15 abandoned. What is her Aban %?
questions.e: Aban % = Aban Calls / Calls Offered = 15 / 405 = 3.7%.

questions.q: Nour answered 390 calls with a THT of 67,306 seconds. What is her AHT?
questions.e: AHT = THT / Calls Answered = 67,306 / 390 = 172.6 seconds.

questions.q: You type 93.3 in a cell and then click the % button. What does Excel show?
questions.e: Excel treats 1 = 100%, so it multiplies 93.3 by 100. Type 0.933 then %, or type 93.3% directly.

questions.q: Login time is in B2 (18:14) and logout time is in C2 (03:20 the next morning). Which formula gives the hours worked?
questions.e: The night shift crosses midnight; MOD(...,1) wraps the negative result around. Answer: 9.10 hours.

questions.q: A call arrives at 13:47. What does =FLOOR(B2,"00:30:00") return?
questions.e: FLOOR rounds DOWN to the half-hour interval: 13:30. This is how WFM builds interval reports. With semicolon regional settings, type =FLOOR(B2;"00:30:00").

questions.q: On the Agents tab, how many Team B agents work the 09:00 - 18:00 shift?
questions.e: =COUNTIFS(Team,"Team B",Shift,"09:00 - 18:00") = 3 (Karim Adel, Farah Wael, Sherif Mounir).

questions.q: =WEEKDAY(A2,2) returns 1 for which day?
questions.e: Return type 2 makes Monday = 1. Without it (type 1), Sunday = 1.

questions.q: You want the highest AHT for Team B only. Which formula works?
questions.e: There is no MAXIF in standard Excel. Use MAXIFS, even with one condition.

questions.q: What is the difference between =SUM(B4,B50) and =SUM(B4:B50)?
o: The comma adds only 2 cells; the colon adds the whole range of 47 cells
questions.e: A comma separates individual cells; a colon creates a continuous range from B4 to B50.

lessons.title: Session test
lessons.note: Formulas here use commas (,) between arguments and a dot for decimals. If your Excel uses semicolons (;) and decimal commas, which is common with Arabic or European regional settings, type those instead.

questions.q: Answered % = C4/B4 shows #DIV/0!. What is the most likely cause?
questions.e: #DIV/0! means dividing by zero or an empty cell. In the trainer's demo, 4 Oct had a blank Offered cell.

questions.q: You typed =SUMM(B3:B11). What error appears?
questions.e: #NAME? means Excel does not recognize the function name. Pick functions from Excel's suggestion list to avoid typos.

questions.q: A lookup returns #N/A although the Login ID looks identical in both tables. Most likely cause?
o: One ID is stored as text or has a hidden space
questions.e: A number in one table and text in the other, or a trailing space, makes the IDs different for Excel.

questions.q: In a nested IF for Excellent / On Target / Below Target, which condition must be tested first?
questions.e: Excel stops at the first TRUE test. If you test >= target first, an Excellent agent is labelled On Target.

questions.q: Mona Fathy has SL 82.2% and is in Team C (target 85%). What is her status?
questions.e: 82.2% is above 80% but Team C's target is 85%. The lookup to the Targets tab makes the status fair per team.

questions.q: In the Dynamic Status Field activity (20 agents), how many are Below Target?
questions.e: Results: 4 Excellent, 6 On Target, 10 Below Target.

questions.q: =VLOOKUP(A2,Agents!A:E,3,FALSE). Which column does it return? (A Login ID, B Name, C Team, D Team Leader, E Shift)
questions.e: Column numbers count inside the table: C is the 3rd column = Team.

questions.q: How do you show "Not Available" when an ID is missing, using XLOOKUP?
questions.e: XLOOKUP's 4th argument is the built-in 'if not found' value. With VLOOKUP you need IFERROR.

questions.q: What does the last argument FALSE (or 0) mean in VLOOKUP?
questions.e: FALSE/0 = exact match, which you need for names, IDs and languages.

questions.q: When do you use HLOOKUP instead of VLOOKUP?
o: When the headers run across a row (horizontal table)
questions.e: HLOOKUP searches the top row of a horizontal table and returns a row number. XLOOKUP can do both.

questions.q: The Data Cleanup Lab has 40 raw rows. How many remain after Remove Duplicates (all columns)?
questions.e: 8 duplicates are removed, leaving 32. Calls Offered drops from 21,089 to 17,072.

questions.q: What does =PROPER(TRIM(" absent ")) return?
o: Absent, with the extra spaces still around it
questions.e: TRIM removes extra spaces and PROPER capitalizes the first letter.

questions.q: Which formula turns the text "31-12-2025" (day-month-year) into a real date on any computer, whatever its regional date settings?
questions.e: DATE(year, month, day) builds the date from the pieces, so it works everywhere. VALUE or DATEVALUE may work on a day-first computer (Egypt, UK) but fail, or swap day and month, on a US-format one. Then format it as Long Date.

questions.q: What does =VALUE(RIGHT("Karim Adel 21002",5)) return?
questions.e: RIGHT takes the last 5 characters; VALUE turns them into a real number.

questions.q: The trainer's rule before running Text to Columns:
o: Insert empty columns / choose an empty destination
questions.e: Otherwise the split overwrites the columns to the right.

questions.q: Why add a Data Validation dropdown (Complete / Pending / In progress)?
o: To stop inconsistent spellings that break analysis
questions.e: "Absent", "absent" and "Absent " count as three different items in filters and pivots.

questions.q: Nested IF risk band: High if Aban % > 5%, Medium if > 3%, else Low. Hossam Ali has 5.1%. Result?
Why does INDEX + MATCH still matter when you have VLOOKUP?
o: It can look left and do two-way lookups in every Excel version
questions.e: INDEX/MATCH returns from any column and can match a row and a column, in all versions.

lessons.title: Session test
lessons.note: Formulas here use commas (,) between arguments and a dot for decimals. If your Excel uses semicolons (;) and decimal commas, which is common with Arabic or European regional settings, type those instead.

questions.q: Manager: "Calls answered by team and by shift." Where does Shift go in the PivotTable?
questions.e: [number] by [Rows] and by [Columns]: Team in Rows, Shift in Columns, Sum of Calls Answered in Values.

questions.q: S5 data (20 agents × 12 weeks): what is the Grand Total of Calls Answered?
questions.e: The PivotTable Builder answer: 121,099.

questions.q: Which team answered the most calls on the 09:00 - 18:00 shift?
questions.e: Team B answered 18,798 calls on 09:00 - 18:00.

questions.q: You changed the source data, but the PivotTable still shows old numbers. What do you do?
questions.e: PivotTables never update by themselves. Right-click > Refresh, or Ctrl+Alt+F5 for all.

questions.q: Team A: 'Average of AHT' in the pivot = 170.7, but the true AHT = 169.0. Why?
o: The pivot averages averages instead of THT / Calls Answered
questions.e: True AHT = total handling time / total calls answered. A busy week must weigh more than a quiet one.

questions.q: How do you get the TRUE team AHT inside the PivotTable?
o: Show Values As > % of Grand Total
questions.e: A calculated field sums each field first, then divides, so it gives the weighted AHT.

questions.q: Grouped by month, August 2026 has the largest share of calls. Why?
o: August has 5 week-start dates in the data
questions.e: July has 4 weeks, August 5, September 3. Always check whether a period comparison is fair.

questions.q: A PivotTable shows 'Count of Calls' instead of 'Sum'. Usual cause?
o: The field has blanks or numbers stored as text
questions.e: Clean the column (Session 2), then re-add the field.

questions.q: Dates will not group by month in the pivot. Why?
o: The dates are stored as text
questions.e: Convert them to real dates first (DATE / Text to Columns).

questions.q: Which chart fits 'weekly calls answered across 12 weeks'?
questions.e: A trend over time = a line chart.

questions.q: Which chart fits the status breakdown (Excellent / On Target / Below Target)?
questions.e: Parts of a whole with only a few slices = a pie chart.

questions.q: Conditional formatting rule 'Aban % greater than 5%': what do you type as the limit?
questions.e: Percent cells hold fractions: 5% = 0.05. Typing 5 means 500%. With decimal-comma regional settings, type 0,05.

questions.q: Dashboard KPI 2: the team AHT (THT / Calls Answered) over 12 weeks is:
questions.e: Total THT / total answered for all 20 agents = 168.5 seconds.

questions.q: Dashboard KPI 3: how many agents are Below Target over the 12 weeks?
questions.e: 5 Excellent, 5 On Target, 10 Below Target.

questions.q: To colour the WHOLE row of a below-target agent, which conditional-formatting formula is right? (Status in column L, data from row 5)
questions.e: Lock the column with $L, keep the row relative so it moves down the table.

questions.q: What controls a PivotChart?
o: The PivotTable it is built on, including its filters
questions.e: Change or filter the pivot and the chart changes with it.

questions.q: Which setting shows each team's share of the total?
o: Show Values As > % of Grand Total
questions.e: Show Values As turns the numbers into shares without any formula.

questions.q: The trainer's advice about using AI tools to write formulas:
o: Use AI, but understand the formula so you can update it later
questions.e: "The objective of this course is that you understand how a formula is written."

lessons.title: Final practical exam
lessons.html:
Open your copy of Activities Workbook .xlsx and build every answer in Excel. Write the formula you used and the result. Time: 60 minutes. Pass mark: 16 / 20 tasks correct. The answer key is in Part 2: check it only after you finish.

Formulas here use commas (,) between arguments and a dot for decimals. If your Excel uses semicolons (;) and decimal commas, which is common with Arabic or European regional settings, type those instead.

A. Reading & formulas (tab S1_Basics / S2_Formulas)

  1. In the Weekly Attendance Export (S1_Basics Part B), write the header row number, the data range and the type of each column.
  2. Hours worked for Dina Gamal (18:14 → 03:20). Show the formula.
  3. Total calls offered by the team (S2_Formulas Part B, rows 53-72).
  4. Longest AHT in the team.
  5. Lowest Service Level %.
  6. For how many agents is a Service Level recorded?
  7. True team AHT = total THT / total calls answered (to 1 decimal).
  8. How many Team A agents work the 18:00 - 03:00 shift? (COUNTIFS on the Agents tab)

B. Logic & lookups (tab S3_Logic_Lookup)

  1. Look up the shift for Login IDs 21003, 99001 and 21018, showing "Not Available" when the ID is missing.
  2. Build the Dynamic Status Field for all 20 agents (Team → SL Target → nested IF). How many agents are Excellent, On Target and Below Target?
  3. Risk band for Rana Ashraf (Aban 4.8%): High > 5%, Medium > 3%, else Low.

C. Cleaning (tab S4_Cleaning)

  1. Convert the text "15-03-2026" into a real date and show it as a long date.
  2. Split "Mahmoud Saeed 21010" into Login ID (number) and Name.
  3. Data Cleanup Lab: how many rows remain after Remove Duplicates, and what is the new Calls Offered total?

D. PivotTables (tab S5_Pivot)

  1. PivotTable: Team in Rows, Shift in Columns, Sum of Calls Answered. Write the Grand Total and Team C's total.
  2. Group Week Start by month. Which month has the largest share, and why is that comparison not fair?
  3. Average of AHT by team vs true AHT by team: write both for Team B.

E. Dashboard (tab S6_Dashboard)

  1. The three KPI numbers: Total Calls Answered, team AHT, Agents Below Target.
  2. Which agents turn RED on Aban % (> 5%) but are still Excellent or On Target on Service Level?
  3. Write your 5-minute presentation headline using the template: "This week the team answered ___ calls at ___ seconds average handling time; ___ agents are below target."
